### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.completion, mini.snippets

### Question

One rough area of my workflow that I've been kicking down the road is making snippets more convenient. I was an early (beta) adopter of mini.snippets and they are great. I am using the lsp server and thus I'm using it with mini.completion. Also notable is that I have the priority for snippets set high (`99`).

What I [believe that I] want is for my snippet expand key (`<c-.>`) to expand snippets no matter what.

The way it works now:
- If I type a prefix like `p` typed and _immediately_ expand it before mini.completion opens the completion list, it expands which is what I want.
- If I type a prefix and wait few ms for mini.completion to open, expanding does nothing. Or rather it types a `.` in the buffer in my case given my expand key.
- If I type a prefix and then navigate to the relevant snippet in the completion list, and _then_ hit my expand key, it works great.
- If I type a prefix, then exit insert mode to close mini.completion, and then enter insert mode again, I'm then in a situation where there is no mini.completion menu and thus the snippet expansion key works as expected.

One thing that kind of does what I'm wanting is to give snippets their default completion priority and use `noinsert` instead of `noselect`, but that's not exactly what I'm looking for either and has other drawbacks.

Can you think of a way to make `<c-.>` expand a snippet whether the completion menu is up or not? I was playing around with some `map_multistep` things and insert mappings but it all feels pretty hacky.

comment_data.body:
I think I might understand the use case and possible solution, but could you please provide more details? Like what snippet prefix do you want to expand (is it literally just `p`?) and what exactly happens in case when it doesn't work (like typing `p` and completion candidates appear, but what candidates are there and what is the inserted text)?

> One thing that kind of does what I'm wanting is to give snippets their default completion priority and use `noinsert` instead of `noselect`, but that's not exactly what I'm looking for either and has other drawbacks.

This sounds a bit strange, since `noselect` does less than `noinsert`. Do you have the means to make a screencast of the problematic usage? And describe what you'd expect.

reply_data.body: You know what, it turns out the problem is that mapping, `<c-.>`. It works decently enough (in the ways I described above) that I never even considered it could be the cause. But if I use something else like `<c-d>` for expanding snippets everything works perfectly with no hiccups whatsoever 😅. Maybe it's an nvim thing or maybe a terminal thing, but it's almost certainly not a mini.nvim thing. Thanks for replying so quickly!
